checked_by: Project maintainer, with AI research assistance (see docs/research-log.md)
notes: Every external link on the site must appear here. 'opened' means the document itself was read on the 'checked' date. 'linked_from' means the address came from another official source and was not opened by our tools. 'guide' says which guide may list or link to a source: a guide's name ('oregon', 'washington', 'utah'), or 'all' for sources any guide may use (federal rules, court papers, standards, national groups, the host). The build goes by 'guide', never by the ID. Kind 'state-explainer' entries are counted for each guide, on its About page, to support the claim that the state explains the rules across more than a dozen documents. The build checks the count only for a guide whose words make that claim; the Washington guide has 9 and does not make it. IDs that start with U are Utah sources, added on 2026-11-10; the letter is only a habit that keeps IDs easy to read. IDs that start with WA are Washington sources, added on 2026-11-12 from a research dossier. A Washington entry with 'opened': false is a real source that was read only in part, through search extracts, or not at all; its 'notes' say which. Until the source review checkpointed for Nov. 26, 2026 is complete, the Washington claims that rest on them are drafting claims (see the 'rules' in data/claims.json and docs/research-log.md). Kind 'state-rule' is a section of a state's administrative code. 'link_check': 'by hand' marks an address whose site blocks automated tools: the weekly link check lists it for a person and does not request it.

sources.title: SMD# 26-006, Optional Hold Harmless Period for Community Engagement Implementation (State Medicaid Director letter)
sources.short: Federal letter to state Medicaid directors, Nov. 13, 2026 (SMD# 26-006)
sources.notes: Read in full on 2026-11-14: 4 pages, 3 footnotes, signed by Daniel Brillman, Deputy Administrator and Director. Offers every state an optional hold harmless period through June 30, 2027. A state that elects it may suspend denials of eligibility and disenrollments when an applicable individual does not demonstrate compliance with community engagement, for applications received and renewals initiated through and including June 30, 2027, or a shorter period the state implements. A state may use the period only if it assesses whether each individual meets the requirement (including deemed compliance) or is excluded, for all relevant applications and renewals in the period. The period covers only conditioning eligibility on community engagement (section 1902(xx)(1) of the Act, 42 C.F.R. 435.559); it does not apply to any other part of implementing community engagement by Jan. 1, 2027, or to denials and disenrollments on other eligibility criteria, such as age or household income. A state requests the period in its mitigation plan and must have CMS approval before using it; a state that intends to use it from Jan. 1, 2027 is asked to notify CMS by Dec. 11, 2026. For applications submitted and renewals initiated after the period ends in a state, the state must deny or terminate eligibility for not meeting the requirement, after the noncompliance procedures at 42 C.F.R. 435.558. The letter does not name any state that has elected the period. Terms: the letter calls the requirement 'community engagement' and says CMS refers to Public Law No. 119-21 as the 'Working Families Tax Cut' (WFTC) legislation. Footnote 3 cites Massachusetts v. Oz as No. 26-12692-RGS; the order in this registry (S28) carries No. 1:26-cv-12962. medicaid.gov answered 403 to a plain automated request on 2026-11-14; the PDF was fetched with a web fetch tool and its text extracted with pdftotext. The CMS press release of the same day is not registered: the letter is the primary source and no page links to the release.

sources.title: What's changing with Apple Health (Medicaid)?
sources.short: HCA client page with the same change table as WA01, plus a note that each H.R. 1 fact sheet is available in 15 languages.
sources.notes: The 15-language statement is on this page. The exact list of fact sheet languages was not verified; the client booklets list at WA09 is verified and is a different list.

sources.title: H.R. 1 impacts
sources.short: HCA stakeholder page on the federal law's effects on Apple Health, including the federal option to delay the work rules to December 31, 2028 by waiver.
sources.date_on_document: No date shown (page content crawled June 18, 2026)
sources.notes: States the delay as an option in the federal law. Does not say Washington has applied for or received it. Also the source for Apple Health being Washington's name for Medicaid and for the near 2 million enrollment figure.

sources.title: Impacts of H.R.1 on Apple Health eligibility - Summary
sources.short: HCA's detailed February 2026 summary of how the eligibility changes will be run: self-attestation, the income test, automatic renewal, and the Verification Hub.
sources.notes: Written before the federal interim final rule issued on June 3, 2026, and says details were pending CMS guidance. Use for Washington's process design, not for federal rule details. Figures: about 602,000 enrolled in Apple Health for Adults in November 2025; about 64 percent estimated verified or exempt from existing data.

sources.title: H.R.1 work requirements and renewals fact sheet
sources.short: HCA's June 2026 fact sheet: who the work rules apply to, the five ways to meet them, the exemption list, and the move from 12-month to 6-month coverage periods.
sources.notes: Read in full from an identical copy hosted by the hospital association after the canonical HCA URL returned HTTP 403 to the crawler. A person must re-open the canonical HCA PDF and confirm the text matches before merge (section 5). This is the single most load-bearing Washington source in the dossier.

sources.title: Apply for or renew coverage
sources.short: HCA page on the ways to apply for or renew Apple Health: online, phone, paper, or in person with a navigator.
sources.notes: Adults under 65 without Medicare apply through Washington Healthplanfinder. Apple Health Classic (65 and older, blindness or disability, Medicare eligible) applies through DSHS and Washington Connection.

sources.title: Contact Apple Health (Medicaid)
sources.short: HCA contact page: MEDS phone line, hours, and mailing address for the MAGI Apple Health programs.
sources.notes: Medical Eligibility Determination Services (MEDS): 1-800-562-3022, Monday to Friday 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Pacific, TRS 711, PO Box 45531, Olympia WA 98504.

sources.title: File an appeal: Apple Health (Medicaid)
sources.short: HCA page on asking for an administrative hearing after an Apple Health decision, through the Office of Administrative Hearings.
sources.notes: Hearing requests go to the Office of Administrative Hearings, online form or 1-800-583-8271. An administrative law judge issues an initial order; the Board of Appeals can review it.

sources.title: Apple Health client booklets
sources.short: HCA page listing Apple Health client booklets in English and 14 other languages.
sources.notes: Languages: Amharic, Arabic, Burmese, Cambodian (Khmer), Chinese, Farsi (Persian), Korean, Laotian, Punjabi, Russian, Somali, Spanish, Tigrigna, Ukrainian, Vietnamese, plus English.

sources.title: Supporting clients with changes to Apple Health
sources.short: HCA Community Connectors page confirming the same H.R. 1 dates and that language assistance is free.
sources.notes: Written for helpers and community organizations. Language assistance includes bilingual staff, interpreters, and translation of printed materials, at no cost.

sources.title: Filing an application
sources.short: HCA page on the paper application form 18-001P and where to fax or send it.
sources.notes: Paper Application for health care coverage, form 18-001P. Fax 1-855-867-4467 as shown on this page. HCA moved this page when it restructured its site; the address was updated and the page re-checked against the facts it supports on Nov. 13, 2026.

sources.title: Changes of circumstance effect on eligibility
sources.short: HCA eligibility manual page on how to report changes and when a reported change takes effect, for Healthplanfinder and Washington Connection cases.
sources.notes: Read through search extracts only. Report a change in Healthplanfinder under Quick Links, by phone to the Healthplanfinder Customer Support Center at 1-855-923-4633 or to MEDS at 1-800-562-3022, by mail to PO Box 946, Olympia WA 98507, or by fax to 360-841-7620. Classic cases report in Washington Connection or at 1-877-501-2233. Must be read in full before the how to apply claims that cite it are published.

sources.title: Submit my verification
sources.short: HCA page on Post Eligibility Reviews: letters asking for proof after an application or renewal, and the 15 days a person has to answer.
sources.notes: Read through search extracts only. Key points: a person must answer a verification letter even if they just updated their information, coverage may close if they do not, and documents can be uploaded in the Healthplanfinder document center.

sources.title: Washington Attorney General's Federal Litigation Tracker
sources.short: The Attorney General's own list of federal cases, including item 62, Commonwealth of Massachusetts v. Oz, the challenge to the federal work requirements rule.
sources.notes: Confirms Washington joined the case on June 29, 2026 with 23 other attorneys general and two governors. Together with the complaint caption (which names Washington as a plaintiff) and shared sources S28 and S40, this establishes that Washington is one of the plaintiff states for the guide's court pages.

sources.title: WAC 182-505-0250, Apple Health for Adults
sources.short: The state rule defining the Apple Health for Adults group: age 19 to 64, no Medicare, Washington resident, income under 138 percent of the federal poverty level.
sources.notes: The eligibility list is quoted in WA05. The rule text itself must be read on the Legislature's site before merge.

sources.title: WAC 182-504-0035, Washington Apple Health renewal reconsideration
sources.short: The state rule giving a person 90 days after a renewal termination to send a completed renewal and get coverage back without a gap, if still eligible.
sources.notes: Read through search extracts only. Also covers reconsideration without a new application when information arrives within 30 days of the termination notice. To be read in full in the source review checkpointed for Nov. 26, 2026.

sources.title: WAC 182-504-0130, Continued coverage pending a hearing
sources.short: The state rule on keeping coverage while an appeal runs: ask for the hearing by the tenth day after the notice was sent or the last day of the month before the action takes effect.
sources.notes: A deadline that falls on a weekend or designated holiday extends to 5:00 p.m. the next business day. To be read in full in the source review checkpointed for Nov. 26, 2026.

sources.title: WAC 182-526-0200, Managed care organization hearing timelines
sources.short: The state rule requiring a person to finish the health plan's grievance and appeal process first, then ask for a hearing within 120 calendar days of the plan's notice of resolution.
sources.notes: Applies when the decision being challenged was made by a managed care organization rather than by HCA. To be read in full in the source review checkpointed for Nov. 26, 2026.

sources.title: WAC 182-503-0080, Hearing rights for application denials
sources.short: The state rule giving a person 90 days from a denial to ask for a hearing, with reconsideration if the agency was wrong.
sources.notes: Read through search extracts only. To be read in full in the source review checkpointed for Nov. 26, 2026.

sources.title: Medicaid in Washington State
sources.short: HCA's January 2026 overview deck on Medicaid in Washington, including the October 1, 2026 noncitizen eligibility changes and the estimate that over 30,000 enrolled people could be affected.
sources.notes: FLAG, naming rule exception: the document's own published title contains the longer form of the state name. It is quoted exactly here because it is a source title. Guide wording must not copy it. Read through search extracts only. The URL is as found in HCA's site index and must be re-verified when the deck is read in full.

sources.title: H.R.1 medically frail memo to providers, with medically frail code list
sources.short: HCA's August 21, 2026 memo to providers on how medical frailty is decided for the work rules, with a published list of qualifying codes.
sources.notes: Not opened. The URL was seen in a secondary source and is unverified. Secondary descriptions say a screening question is answered in Washington Healthplanfinder, self-attestation is accepted through 2027, and the state checks its own records first from January 2028 with a 12-month look-back. None of that may be published until this memo and the code list are read in full.

sources.title: Apple Health (Medicaid) work requirements
sources.short: HCA's main client page on the work requirements, with a short screener survey, at the short address hca.wa.gov/ah-work-req.
sources.notes: The text fetch returned an empty page on 2026-11-12, so the page's own wording has not been read. This is the page most likely to change the checker design. It is to be read in full in the source review checkpointed for Nov. 26, 2026.

sources.title: Apple Health Expansion
sources.short: HCA page on the state-funded coverage program on Washington Healthplanfinder for adults who do not qualify for federally funded Apple Health, including its enrollment limit.
sources.notes: Read through search extracts only. As of the December 2025 update, enrollment was closed because the enrollment limit was met. Must be re-read before the immigration page is built, because closed enrollment changes what the guide may suggest.

sources.title: Medicaid Community Engagement Requirement for Certain Individuals, Interim Final Rule with Comment Period (CMS-2454-IFC), fact sheet
sources.short: The CMS fact sheet issued with the interim final rule, including the list of short-term hardship categories a state may adopt.
sources.publisher: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services
sources.notes: Read in part through search extracts. The rule itself is already in the registry as shared source S27 and stays the primary federal source. This fact sheet is proposed for the hardship category list only. The build may prefer to cite S27 alone.

sources.title: Complaint, Commonwealth of Massachusetts v. Oz, No. 1:26-cv-12962 (D. Mass.)
sources.short: The filed complaint in the states' challenge to the federal work requirements rule. The caption names Washington as a plaintiff.
sources.notes: Read through search extracts, including the caption and plaintiff list. The judgment, order, and docket are already tracked as shared sources S28, S29, and S40. This entry exists so Washington claims can cite Washington's own plaintiff status without relying on another guide's sources.

application_languages.notes: Paper OHP application (form 7210) links as listed on OHA's how-to-apply page on 2026-11-02. 'native' is OHA's own label in that language where OHA gave one; it is marked up with the matching lang attribute. 'english' is the language name in English. 'hreflang' describes the linked document.
